session.question: How was ARDL used to test the nexus, and what long-run association did it reveal for human capital and renewable energy?
session.answer:
The nexus was tested using a cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) / ARDL framework applied to panel data, with the method chosen for its robustness to heterogeneity, fractional integration, endogeneity, and cross-sectional dependence. In the ASEAN study, this approach was used to estimate both short-run and long-run relationships among human capital, green/renewable energy, and environmental quality measured by the load capacity factor. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1)

The ARDL results revealed a statistically meaningful long-run association in which human capital expanded the load capacity factor and improved environmental quality, while renewable/green energy also stimulated the load capacity factor. In substantive terms, this indicates that higher human capital and greater renewable energy use are linked to better environmental outcomes over the long run. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1)

A related CS-ARDL study in emerging economies similarly found that green energy and the human capital index reduce environmental degradation in both the long run and the short run, reinforcing the long-run beneficial role of both variables. (huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-320c52cb: The paper uses panel data for the top eight advanced economies from 1990 to 2018 and applies an advanced panel technique, specifically cross-sectionally augmented distributed lags (CS-ARDL), to estimate both long-run and short-run relationships among green technologies, clean energy, environmental taxes, and human well-being. The abstract states that the CS-ARDL estimation confirms a productive impact of green technologies on environmental and human well-being, and that clean energy contributes to a sustainable environment and human development in the long run. Renewable/clean energy is therefore presented as positively associated with human development over the long term.
From Nguyen Binh An, Yen-Lin Kuo, Fatma Mabrouk, Shouvik Sanyal, Iskandar Muda, Sanil S. Hishan, and Niamat Abdulrehman. Ecological innovation for environmental sustainability and human capital development: the role of environmental regulations and renewable energy in advanced economies. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2022.2120046, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2022.2120046.

pqac-1f2a9c53: The paper uses a cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) approach to study emerging economies from 1995–2018. It reports that there exists cross-sectional dependence (CSD), cointegration, and slope heterogeneity among the variables. The CS-ARDL results indicate that economic growth raises carbon emissions in both the long and short run, while green energy and the human capital index have a constructive effect in lowering environmental degradation in both long-run and short-run estimations. This provides evidence of a long-run association between the variables, especially the beneficial long-run role of human capital and green energy.
From Shi‐Zheng Huang, Fengsheng Chien, and Muhammad Sadiq. A gateway towards a sustainable environment in emerging countries: the nexus between green energy and human capital. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2021.2012218, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2021.2012218.

pqac-50b0c351: The study examined ASEAN data from 1986–2018 using a cross-sectionally augmented ARDL approach, chosen to be robust to heterogeneity, fractional integration, endogeneity, and cross-sectional dependence. It tested the nexus between human capital (HUC), green/renewable energy (GEN), and environmental quality via the load capacity factor (LCF) within the load capacity curve framework. The ARDL results showed a long-run positive association: human capital expands LCF and promotes environmental quality, and green energy also stimulates LCF. In short, the model revealed that higher human capital and renewable/green energy are linked to improved environmental outcomes in the long run.
From Jiapeng Dai, Zahoor Ahmed, Rafael Alvarado, and Mahmood Ahmad. Assessing the nexus between human capital, green energy, and load capacity factor: policymaking for achieving sustainable development goals. Gondwana Research, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009, doi:10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009.

pqac-1a18a54e: The paper uses a cross-sectionally augmented ARDL approach, described as robust to heterogeneity, fractional integration, endogeneity, and cross-sectional dependence (CSD). It analyzes ASEAN data from 1986–2018 within the load capacity curve (LCC) framework. The results indicate a long-run relationship where human capital (HUC) expands the load capacity factor and promotes environmental quality, and green energy also stimulates LCF. The abstract suggests these findings support a long-run association between human capital, renewable/green energy, and environmental quality.
From Jiapeng Dai, Zahoor Ahmed, Rafael Alvarado, and Mahmood Ahmad. Assessing the nexus between human capital, green energy, and load capacity factor: policymaking for achieving sustainable development goals. Gondwana Research, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009, doi:10.1016/j.gr.2023.04.009.

pqac-449b231c: The paper uses secondary data for China from 1986 to 2019 and applies the augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test to check stationarity, followed by an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model to test the relationships among variables. The abstract reports that human capital index and renewable energy consumption/production are negatively associated with carbon emissions and positively associated with SDG, implying a long-run association in the ARDL framework. The study frames these results as evidence for policy guidance on sustainable development goals.
From Mingqi Zhu. The role of human capital and environmental protection on the sustainable development goals: new evidences from chinese economy. Economic Research-Ekonomska Istraživanja, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/1331677x.2022.2113334, doi:10.1080/1331677x.2022.2113334.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How was ARDL used to test the nexus, and what long-run association did it reveal for human capital and renewable energy?

The nexus was tested using a cross-sectionally augmented autoregressive distributed lag (CS-ARDL) / ARDL framework applied to panel data, with the method chosen for its robustness to heterogeneity, fractional integration, endogeneity, and cross-sectional dependence. In the ASEAN study, this approach was used to estimate both short-run and long-run relationships among human capital, green/renewable energy, and environmental quality measured by the load capacity factor. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1)

The ARDL results revealed a statistically meaningful long-run association in which human capital expanded the load capacity factor and improved environmental quality, while renewable/green energy also stimulated the load capacity factor. In substantive terms, this indicates that higher human capital and greater renewable energy use are linked to better environmental outcomes over the long run. (dai2023assessingthenexus chunk 1)

A related CS-ARDL study in emerging economies similarly found that green energy and the human capital index reduce environmental degradation in both the long run and the short run, reinforcing the long-run beneficial role of both variables. (huang2021agatewaytowards chunk 1)
